openingLines: Keep the pavement clean and your papers in order. That is how we get through this.
Morning. Have you taken your prescribed tablets?
The patrols are protecting us. Please do not interfere with their work.

tablet-response.text: Thank you very much, kind sir. Please give Nadia my heartfelt thanks as well. It is a great comfort to know that someone is looking out for us.

courier-pickup-confirmed.text: Take this parcel to the recipient named in your journal.

courier-delivery-thanks.text: Thank you. Here is your payment.

find-item-instructions.text: Find the requested item and take it to the recipient in your journal.

find-item-payment.text: Exactly what was requested. Here is your payment.

greeting.text: Elena Jovanovic. I clean the streets and look after the buildings. There is enough work without people spreading rumors. What do you need? Nadia keeps telling me to take my tablets, and I do. There is no shame in following medical advice.

choices.text: [Medicine] Nadia sent me with a white tablet for you.
[Courier] I am here to collect the parcel.
[Find item] Tell me about your request.
[Find item] I found the requested item.
What do you think of the quarantine?
Did you receive your tablets from Nadia?
I want to ask about something strange.
Can you tell me about a specific person?

town-opinion.text: The capital has sent soldiers and medicine. That is more than enough proof they mean to help us. People who complain should try keeping these streets clean for a week. That student Milena keeps asking after her parents. I feel sorry for the girl, but shouting at officials will not bring anyone home.

tablet.text: Of course I took mine. Nadia works hard to bring them. People who refuse treatment only make things worse for their neighbors.

about.text: I have spent years sweeping these streets. I know who keeps their steps tidy and who leaves trouble behind. I go home before curfew, as everyone should.

ask-about.text: Strange? There is nothing strange about a town under medical quarantine. But go on.

choices.text: Have you ever seen anything unusual after dark?
What about people who have disappeared?

night.text: Once I thought I saw something tall between the buildings. But it was dark, and I had missed a tablet. Nadia says the illness can deceive the eyes. I stay inside at night now.

disappear.text: If someone has been taken for treatment, it is for their own good. Do you think the soldiers enjoy doing that? I do not ask questions that might interfere with their duty.

people-menu.text: Who? I know most of the people in this town. Some better than they would like.

people-about-pavel-sokolov.text: Mr. Sokolov came from the capital. He knows what needs doing, and he has more patience than this town deserves. I tell him when people spread dangerous nonsense. It's a civic duty, not gossip.

people-about-dusan-markovic.text: Dusan? Always complaining, always smelling of spirits. He won't take the tablets, then wonders why he sees things in the dark. I keep an eye on him. Someone has to.

people-about-irina-kovalenko.text: Irina works hard at the factory. A respectable woman, though she asks too many questions about missing materials. The capital has its reasons for every allocation.

people-about-viktor-petrov.text: Viktor serves people who ought to be home resting. His bar is where rumors breed. He can be kind, I suppose, but kindness isn't an excuse for encouraging disobedience.

people-about-zofia-nowak.text: Zofia keeps a proper shop. She follows the distribution notices exactly, and she doesn't indulge every complaint. We need more people like her.

people-about-milena-vukovic.text: That university girl, Milena, came back full of questions. Her parents' troubles are sad, truly. But accusing the authorities won't bring them home. I wish she'd listen.

people-about-nadia-morozova.text: Nadia is a blessing. She brings our tablets even when people insult her for it. I told her I saw a figure outside once; she said the illness can play tricks. That settled it for me.

postman-thanks.text: Thank you for bringing my letter.
